maria (infra): FYI I'm about to land a Terraform change that tweaks HPA targets for inference-worker svc in staging. Seeing oscillation when combined with VPA autoscale mode:Auto. Can someone quick-check the plan?

aj (platform): thx — can you paste the tf diff and the HPA manifest? also which autoscaler is active in staging, CA or Karpenter?

maria (infra): plan snippet: ```hcl
module "k8s_apps" {
  source = "git::ssh://.../tf-k8s-modules.git//hpa"
  hpa_cpu_target = 45
  min_replicas   = 2
  max_replicas   = 30
}
```
And the k8s HPA (generated by the module): ```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-worker
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference-worker
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics:
  - type:Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 45
```
We also have a VPA object in the same namespace (mode: Auto) and Karpenter is enabled (provisioner present) but Cluster Autoscaler is disabled for our nodegroup clusters.

sanjay: mixing VPA Auto + HPA can be rough — VPA changes requests which shifts HPA behaviour. For inference workloads I'd recommend VPA mode: "Auto" only for non-HPA workloads. Consider VPA mode: "Off" and serve resource recommendations via Recommender only.

leah: agree. Another option: set HPA based on custom metrics (qps or queue depth) instead of CPU, so VPA recommendations don't move the goalposts.

maria (infra): good point. We used CPU since it's easy, but real signal is redis queue length. We have a metrics-server and custom-metrics adapter in staging. Quick q: is there a recommended terraform var name for toggling VPA in the charts so we can test without infra churn?

aj (platform): we already have a var in the helm chart values: `vpa.enabled` (bool). You can set that via module var: `vpa_enabled = false` in your staging workspace. Example in Terraform:
```
module "inference_chart" {
  source = ".../helm_release_module"
  values = [file("values.yaml"), jsonencode({ vpa = { enabled = false } })]
}
```
That will render without touching node provisioning.

maria (infra): perfect. Will toggle in staging and redeploy. Any Karpenter tunables to watch? We're seeing a lot of small nodes spin up then get consolidated out, which is fine but causing pod churn.

sanjay: check Provisioner settings: `consolidation.enabled = true` and `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` and `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` matter. If TTL is too short it will terminate nodes quickly and cause churn. Example values we use: `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300` and `consolidation: { enabled: true }`. Also look at `limits.resources` so Karpenter prefers packed nodes.

leah: also watch out for Karpenter's topology spread — if your pods have constraints that force distribution, you get many small nodes. If inference-worker tolerates bin-packing, relax anti-affinity.

maria (infra): noted. One more: secrets/wiring — Karpenter needs permissions for creating EC2 instances and tagging. I updated the iam role module; will include the KMS key arn for node encryption. Anything else to add?

aj (platform): ensure the instance profile role has `ec2:CreateFleet`, `iam:PassRole`, and the Node bootstrap user data can access SSM params if you store bootstrap scripts there. For KMS, add the key to the role policy: `kms:Decrypt` for the node role if it needs to unwrap secrets.

deploy-bot: deploy started by @maria (infra) — plan ok, no deletions for prod. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

maria (infra): rolling to staging now with `vpa_enabled = false` + HPA still on CPU for quick test. I'll monitor scale metrics and post back. If stable we'll make a small RFC to change default to `vpa.enabled = false` for HPA'd apps.

aj (platform): thanks — ping here when you have graphs, if we need to revert fast add a feature flag or a terraform workspace pin.

maria (infra): will do. current plan summary in the PR: disable VPA in staging, set karpenter ttlSecondsAfterEmpty = 300 in staging provisioner, and change HPA metric to queue depth if stable. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

sanjay: if you need a quick script to convert CPU-based HPA to queue-metric HPA I can drop one here.

maria (infra): please, that'd help. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
